messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
Cyclobenzaprine acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Cyclobenzaprine will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of central nervous system disease include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show Cyclobenzaprine blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of Cyclobenzaprine's side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
Triples: [["Cyclobenzaprine", "has mechanism of action", "reducing nerve signals in the brain"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "reduces", "nerve signals in the brain"], ["nerve signals in the brain", "drive", "muscle tone and spasm"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "allows", "tight, overactive muscles to relax"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "acts in", "central nervous system"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "acts primarily at", "brain stem"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "does not act on", "muscles themselves"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "does not act at", "junction between nerves and muscle"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has mechanism of action", "working through the nervous system"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "will not relieve", "muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease"], ["central nervous system disease", "includes", "cerebral palsy"], ["central nervous system disease", "includes", "spinal cord disease"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "mechanism of action in", "fibromyalgia is not known"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "blocks", "serotonin (5-HT2A) receptor"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "blocks", "histamine receptor"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "blocks", "muscarinic receptor"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "is chemically related to", "tricyclic antidepressants"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "is chemically related to", "amitriptyline"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has side effect", "drowsiness"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has side effect", "dry mouth"]]
Relations: ["acts in", "acts primarily at", "allows", "blocks", "does not act at", "does not act on", "drive", "has mechanism of action", "has side effect", "includes", "is chemically related to", "mechanism of action in", "reduces", "will not relieve"]
Answer:

completion:
acts in: The subject drug exerts its effects within the anatomical or physiological system specified by the object entity.  
acts primarily at: The subject drug exerts its primary effects at the anatomical or physiological location specified by the object entity.  
allows: The subject drug enables the physiological process or function specified by the object entity.  
blocks: The subject drug inhibits or prevents the activity of the receptor or pathway specified by the object entity.  
does not act at: The subject drug does not exert its effects at the anatomical or physiological location specified by the object entity.  
does not act on: The subject drug does not exert its effects directly on the anatomical or physiological entity specified by the object entity.  
drive: The subject physiological process or entity is responsible for initiating or maintaining the function or condition specified by the object entity.  
has mechanism of action: The subject drug operates through the physiological or biochemical process specified by the object entity.  
has side effect: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or reaction specified by the object entity.  
includes: The subject category or class contains the specific entity or example specified by the object entity.  
is chemically related to: The subject drug shares a chemical structure or pharmacological similarity with the drug or class specified by the object entity.  
mechanism of action in: The subject drug's mechanism of action in the specified condition or disease is not known.  
reduces: The subject drug decreases or diminishes the activity or intensity of the physiological process or entity specified by the object entity.  
will not relieve: The subject drug is ineffective in alleviating or treating the condition or symptom specified by the object entity.
